rankings.summaryHtml: Maybe that 69-65 slugfest with short-handed OKC -- just the 11th time in the shot-clock era that the winning team scored 69 points or fewer -- was by design to save as much offense as the Rockets could for Monday's visit to Memphis. They'll surely need every last point against the stingy Grizz.

rankings.summaryHtml: A flashy start is new ground for the Grizz, who somehow find themselves over .500 after 10 games for just the third time in the club's two-decade history. Now Memphis hosts Houston having won 19 in a row at home, after the Courtney Lee-capped comeback from 26 down to Sacramento saved that streak.

rankings.summaryHtml: Surely the Dubs were disappointed that they failed to handle San Antonio when the Spurs were (A) on the road and (B) on the second night of a back-to-back. rankings.summaryHtml: Cannot tell a lie: There was some second-guessing by the committee (of one) after dropping the Spurs only to No. 7 amid just the fifth sub-.500 start through five games for any reigning champ since the NBA/ABA merger in '76-77. rankings.summaryHtml: If you think the committee can't find a silver lining to a 1-9 start, think again. Despite what you've heard, Kobe is actually fifth all-time in most misses once you add in errant FTs. That takes him to 15,030 career misses, behind Wilt (16,621), Mailman (16,083), Elvin Hayes (15,939) and Kareem (15,062).
